verses.1: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.
verses.2: In the seventh year Jehu reigned, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah, from Beer-sheba.
verses.3: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days, as Jehoida the priest instructed him.
verses.4: Yet the high places still stood, and the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense on the high places.
verses.5: Joash said to the priests, "All the sacred money brought into the house of the LORD—each person’s sacred offering, the money for the redemption of souls, the money for any offering a person brings into the house of the LORD—
verses.6: let the priests take some from each of your earnings, and they shall use it to repair the house of the LORD in whatever place they find it damaged."
verses.7: But in the twenty-third year of King Joash’s reign, the priests had still not repaired the damage to the house.
verses.8: Then the king summoned Jehoida the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the house? From now on, do not take any money from your earnings, but give it all to the repair of the house."
verses.9: The priests agreed not to take money from the people or to repair the damage to the house.
verses.10: Jehoida the priest took a chest, cut a hole in its lid, and placed it near the altar on the right side of the temple entrance. The priests who guarded the threshold collected the money that came into the house of the LORD.
verses.11: When they saw the large amount of money in the chest, the king’s scribe and the high priest came and counted the money found in the house of the LORD.
verses.12: They gave the money collected to the workers in charge of the house of the LORD. They paid the carpenters, the masons, and the others working on the house of the LORD.
verses.13: They also paid the stonemasons and the laborers to buy timber and dressed stone to repair the house of the LORD and to cover any work needed for its restoration.
verses.14: But they were not to make any gold or silver items for the house of the LORD—no doors, clasps, or bowls, no gold or silver vessels from the money brought into the house of the LORD.
verses.15: Instead, the money was to be given to the workers, to repair the house of the LORD.
verses.16: They did not count the people who gave the money to the workers, because they trusted the people to give honestly.
verses.17: No money for guilt offerings or for sin offerings brought into the house of the LORD was given to the priests.
verses.18: Then Hazael, king of Aram, came up and attacked Gath. He captured it and set his face to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.19: King Joash took all the sacred offerings that his ancestors—Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, the kings of Judah—had dedicated, along with his own sacred items and all the gold he found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the king’s house. He sent it to Hazael, king of Aram, and Hazael withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.20: The rest of the events of Joash, all that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
verses.21: His servants conspired and killed him in the house of Millo, as he was coming down from Silla.
verses.22: Joazad the son of Shimath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, struck him down and he died. They buried him with his ancestors in the city of David, and his son Amaziah became king in his place.

notes:
Notes
- v. 17: The reference to "money for guilt offerings or for sin offerings" is based on the context of temple offerings and the separation of funds for different purposes, though the precise term for "sin offerings" is not explicitly used in the source.
raw:
[1] Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.
[2] In the seventh year Jehu reigned, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah, from Beer-sheba.
[3] Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days, as Jehoida the priest instructed him.
[4] Yet the high places still stood, and the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense on the high places.
[5] Joash said to the priests, "All the sacred money brought into the house of the LORD—each person’s sacred offering, the money for the redemption of souls, the money for any offering a person brings into the house of the LORD—
[6] let the priests take some from each of your earnings, and they shall use it to repair the house of the LORD in whatever place they find it damaged."
[7] But in the twenty-third year of King Joash’s reign, the priests had still not repaired the damage to the house.
[8] Then the king summoned Jehoida the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the house? From now on, do not take any money from your earnings, but give it all to the repair of the house."
[9] The priests agreed not to take money from the people or to repair the damage to the house.
[10] Jehoida the priest took a chest, cut a hole in its lid, and placed it near the altar on the right side of the temple entrance. The priests who guarded the threshold collected the money that came into the house of the LORD.
[11] When they saw the large amount of money in the chest, the king’s scribe and the high priest came and counted the money found in the house of the LORD.
[12] They gave the money collected to the workers in charge of the house of the LORD. They paid the carpenters, the masons, and the others working on the house of the LORD.
[13] They also paid the stonemasons and the laborers to buy timber and dressed stone to repair the house of the LORD and to cover any work needed for its restoration.
[14] But they were not to make any gold or silver items for the house of the LORD—no doors, clasps, or bowls, no gold or silver vessels from the money brought into the house of the LORD.
[15] Instead, the money was to be given to the workers, to repair the house of the LORD.
[16] They did not count the people who gave the money to the workers, because they trusted the people to give honestly.
[17] No money for guilt offerings or for sin offerings brought into the house of the LORD was given to the priests.
[18] Then Hazael, king of Aram, came up and attacked Gath. He captured it and set his face to go up to Jerusalem.
[19] King Joash took all the sacred offerings that his ancestors—Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, the kings of Judah—had dedicated, along with his own sacred items and all the gold he found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the king’s house. He sent it to Hazael, king of Aram, and Hazael withdrew from Jerusalem.
[20] The rest of the events of Joash, all that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
[21] His servants conspired and killed him in the house of Millo, as he was coming down from Silla.
[22] Joazad the son of Shimath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, struck him down and he died. They buried him with his ancestors in the city of David, and his son Amaziah became king in his place.
